findings.control: Start from real finalized unknown-generation evidence; inject an edge mutation in the semantic scan boundary, and require recorded replay to refuse rather than return a qualified view. Preserve the prior source report and raw generation.
findings.minimal_fix: Capture the selected edge file with the same admission before scanning it, then retain the existing guard verification. Do not bind writable producer outputs into the raw-generation guard before legitimate source finalization.
findings.observation: Recorded replay currently scans the source edge file with _check_omitted_assertions but does not itself capture that edge file in its SourceAdmission before the semantic read.
findings.risk: This helper relies on surrounding generic graph-member checks instead of retaining an explicit identity for the exact graph bytes whose unknown/empty omission semantics it inspects. A mutation during that local semantic-read window is not necessarily observed by this helper's own guard.verify. No production false-admission bypass has been demonstrated.

findings.control: From a real run, replace cached audit bytes to relabel unknown_unavailable as explicit_empty (or alter a head identity), then require verify_native_inputs/finalization/write to fail without emitting a new completed audit or receipt.
findings.minimal_fix: Regenerate _audit_bytes(_rows(view)) inside _verify_cache and require exact equality to the original cached _audit. Retain exact view/record/state checks and replay.
findings.observation: The consumer retains canonical generation/qualification/record identities, but private cached _audit bytes are used by write()/contract() without regenerating and comparing them to validated endpoint records at each boundary.
findings.risk: Replacing cached audit bytes can influence producer-written audit and its contract hash even while endpoint evidence remains unchanged. Independent public replay already regenerates the audit and rejects a semantic mismatch, but producer completion should refuse the mutation first.

related_strict_type_finding.observation: Python dictionary equality can equate JSON boolean/integer or integer/float contract values. Use canonical strict JSON comparisons, not value-coercing container equality, and add sealed1/coverage-count-type controls.
